This is bigger than just fishing a rocket out of the ocean.

Flight 13’s Starship is the first to survive a controlled reentry and soft splashdown intact — and stay floating long enough for recovery.
That means engineers can finally put their hands on real flight hardware: heat shield tiles that endured peak heating, engines that fired through the landing burn, and flaps that guided it hypersonic.

Every previous Ship was lost. This one can teach us exactly what worked, what didn’t, and how to make Starship truly reusable.
The data from this recovery could accelerate the path to tower catches and rapid turnaround more than any telemetry ever could.

That’s why the recovery team is fighting rough seas right now.
History in the making. 🚀

Tesla and SpaceX are making one of the largest industrial investments in Texas. 

Here's what the two companies are building across the state:

• Terafab (Grimes County)
• Gigasat factory (Bastrop – under construction)
• Optimus factory (Giga Texas – under construction)
• Advanced Technology Fab (Giga Texas – under construction)
• Tesla Project Crystal Sun – a major solar cell plant in Fort Bend County (construction expected to begin in late 2026)
• Expanded Starlink terminal production facility (Bastrop – under construction)
• Continued expansion of Starbase
• Tesla Megafactory 3 (Brookshire – production has already begun)

The scale of manufacturing and infrastructure being built across Texas is unlike anything Tesla and SpaceX have undertaken before.

It’s no longer about cool demos. It’s about scaling AI from pilots into everyday workflows that deliver real ROI.We sat down with Bob Sakalas from @SAP, Bo English-Wiczling from @PayPal, and Ariel Shulman from Bright Data.

They all pointed to the same shift — the companies that win will be the ones that successfully move AI from individual tools and experiments into core business processes that people rely on every day.

AI only creates lasting value when it stops being a side project and starts becoming part of everyday work.

People love to hate on California.

High taxes, traffic, housing costs, and visible problems are real. The trade-offs exist. So do the upsides.

UP (@UnpluggedTesla)

Built to the full extent of the UP INVINCIBLE® program. Finished like nothing else on the road.

This customer's FlexiShield Dune-colored PPF-wrapped Cybertruck blends into desert sand and stands apart from everything else. 

Underneath the finish is the complete Stage 3 Expedition and Pursuit build, engineered for dry lakebeds, rock, and long-distance expedition use. Steel replaces factory plastic at every corner: heavy-duty front bumper, bull bar, rock sliders, and a rear bumper with integrated hitch that raises the departure angle to 30.7 degrees.

Four lighting systems, 154 inches of native 48-volt LED, layered at four heights to eliminate blind ground ahead of the truck. The roof-mounted 50-inch double-row bar alone delivers 38,400 raw lumens with a beam reaching beyond 3,000 feet.

A pre-preg carbon-fiber, Kevlar-reinforced hood with an integrated curved 50-inch bar sits above 20x9 UP-03 Beadlocks wrapped in BFGoodrich KO3s, with satin dry carbon wide-body flares adding 2.3 inches of track width. CYBRSHOCKS rear secondary shocks and a three-way adjustable rear sway bar keep it all under control.

Every part on this truck is a catalog part. Any Cybertruck owner can build this exact spec, one component at a time or in one step.

Terafab just got real.

Tesla + SpaceX confirmed the full-scale chip factory in Grimes County, Texas.
≈100–110 million square feet

Thousands of acres

For perspective, here’s the true scale against the largest chip factories that actually exist today:
• Giga Texas → ~10M sq ft
• TSMC Fab 18 (Taiwan) → ~10.2M sq ft
• TSMC Arizona (first building) → ~3.5M sq ft
• Samsung Taylor → ~2.7–4M sq ft
Terafab is in a completely different category.
